title: Expanding Capabilities to Combat Transnational Cyber-Enabled Crime

MEMORANDUM FOR THE VICE PRESIDENT

THE SECRETARY OF STATE

THE SECRETARY OF THE TREASURY

THE SECRETARY OF WAR

THE ATTORNEY GENERAL

THE SECRETARY OF COMMERCE

THE SECRETARY OF ENERGY

THE SECRETARY OF HOMELAND SECURITY

THE ASSISTANT TO THE PRESIDENT AND CHIEF OF STAFF

THE DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE

THE ASSISTANT TO THE PRESIDENT FOR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

THE DIRECTOR OF THE CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY

THE DIRECTOR OF THE OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET

THE ASSISTANT TO THE PRESIDENT FOR NATIONAL SECURITY AFFAIRS

THE ASSISTANT TO THE PRESIDENT AND DEPUTY CHIEF OF STAFF FOR POLICY AND HOMELAND SECURITY ADVISOR

THE NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR

THE CHAIRMAN OF THE JOINT CHIEFS OF STAFF

THE DIRECTOR OF THE NATIONAL SECURITY AGENCY

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby direct the following:

Section 1.  Purpose.  Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs) pose a growing threat to American citizens, businesses, and national security.  These organizations conduct sustained cyber campaigns to perpetrate frauds that undermine American prosperity, security, and freedom.  Through Executive Order 14390 of March 6, 2026 (Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens), I directed the Federal Government to take various actions to combat cyber‑enabled crime harming American citizens.  This memorandum expands the fight against TCO-perpetrated cybercrime by incorporating the ingenuity of the private sector. 

The American private sector is the most innovative and technologically advanced in the world, and its scale, speed, and capacity secure a critical offensive cyber advantage for the United States.  Yet, American businesses’ innovative capabilities have historically been underutilized in efforts to identify and disrupt criminal networks operating in cyberspace.  Thus, it is the policy of the United States to use all instruments of national power, including the innovative capabilities of the private sector, to combat cybercrime.  By partnering with vetted United States companies subject to the direction and oversight of the Federal Government, we will enhance our ability to counter TCO threats and combat transnational cybercrime, fraud, and other predatory schemes against American citizens.

Sec. 2.  Establishing the Program.  (a)  The National Coordination Center (NCC), established pursuant to section 6(d) of Executive Order 14159 of January 20, 2025 (Protecting the American People Against Invasion), shall create, manage, and maintain a Program to authorize Participating Companies, as defined in section 4(f) of this memorandum, to conduct Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations against foreign Cyber-Enabled Transnational Criminal Organizations (CE-TCOs), under the control and oversight of the Federal Government.  As part of lawful investigatory, protective, or intelligence operations carried out by Federal law enforcement, this Program shall:

(i)    be overseen by co-Executive Directors, one from the Department of Justice, designated by the Attorney General, and one from the Department of Homeland Security, designated by the Secretary of Homeland Security (Program Executive Directors).  The Program Executive Directors shall be delegated authority to approve, after coordination with each other, cyber operations conducted within the Program by personnel of their respective departments, except that they may not approve operations resulting in Critical Outcomes, as defined in section 4(b) of this memorandum.  Cyber operations shall only be approved after coordination between the Program Executive Directors, and any resulting operational action will be exclusively conducted on behalf of and under the supervision of the Federal Government pursuant to the Federal Government’s lawful authorities;

(ii)   require Participating Companies to enter into contractual agreements with the Department of Justice or the Department of Homeland Security, which shall ensure that Participating Companies undergo rigorous vetting and that their performance adheres to the strict operational procedures outlined in the implementation guidance directed in section 3 of this memorandum; and

(iii)  permit Participating Companies to enter into commercial agreements with:

(A)  private sector entities, from which the Participating Companies may receive for the purpose of proposing responsive cyber operations to the NCC any threat information collected in the course of those entities’ normal business activities; and

(B)  Federal, State, local, tribal, and territorial agencies, which will identify CE-TCO threats to the Participating Companies in a manner that enables them to propose cyber operations to the NCC that address those threats.

(b)  The NCC shall conduct all Program activities in accordance with the Constitution and all other applicable laws and international obligations of the United States, including section 1030 of title 18, United States Code, thereby ensuring that Participating Companies are acting under the control and oversight of the United States Government.

Sec. 3.  Implementing Guidance.  (a)  Within 60 days of the date of this memorandum, the Program Executive Directors shall, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, establish consensus operating procedures for the Program that ensure the Federal Government’s complete oversight and control of Participating Companies’ performance.  No operation may be approved unless it complies with these operating procedures.  The procedures shall:

(i)     establish minimum standards that Participating Companies must meet in order to take part in the Program, which shall include appropriate levels of technical proficiency, proven performance of cyber operations, facility security, personnel vetting, competence, reliability, and other factors that the Program Executive Directors, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, determine are relevant or necessary for guaranteeing high confidence in a Participating Company’s ability to perform successfully in the Program;

(ii)    ensure that the Program’s eligibility criteria enable participation by both large companies, which provide critical capacity, and smaller, more agile companies, which may be better suited for specialized or discrete tasks;

(iii)   mandate that Participating Companies disclose to the NCC all contractual relationships entered into pursuant to section 2(a)(iii) of this memorandum;

(iv)    authorize the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security to mandate as a condition of their contractual agreements with Participating Companies under section 2(a)(ii) of this memorandum that such companies maintain a bond or escrow in an amount not less than $1 million, to be forfeited should the Participating Company enter non‑compliance with its contractual agreement described in section 2(a)(ii) of this memorandum;

(v)     in conformance with the classified annex to this memorandum, set forth the operational workflow of the Program, which shall include operational deconfliction across Federal law enforcement, the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, the Department of War, the Department of Justice, and the United States Intelligence Community;

(vi)    in conformance with the classified annex to this memorandum, provide an adjudicatory framework to ensure operational activity targets only CE-TCOs and accounts for other United States Government equities;

(vii)   set forth standardized rubrics and templates for target identification and the creation and processing of Cyber Surveillance and Cyber Effects Operations packages;

(viii)  include reporting requirements for Participating Companies that will advance a greater understanding of the activities and impact of foreign CE-TCOs, especially as they relate to the American people and economy, and that will ensure the NCC is fully apprised of the Participating Companies’ operational activities;

(ix)    include procedures, including a review by the Department of Justice, that ensure any Program activity that is directed at a United States person or otherwise implicates the United States Government’s obligations under the Constitution, Federal law, or international law receives any necessary authorization, judicial or otherwise, prior to approval of the operation;

(x)     include procedures to ensure that a Participating Company that discovers operational activity exceeding the parameters and restrictions of the cyber operation approved by the Program Executive Directors — such as unintentional targeting of (1) a United States person, (2) an information system residing in the United States, or (3) an information system under the control of a United States person — shall cease such operation, conduct minimization procedures, and immediately notify the NCC, which shall notify the Department of Justice;

(xi)    include procedures mandating that Participating Companies immediately notify the NCC, which shall notify the Department of Justice, if they discover an imminent cyber-attack against United States critical infrastructure or develop a reasonable belief that an approved Cyber Effects Operation or Cyber Surveillance Operation may result in Critical Outcomes;

(xii)   clarify that Participating Companies may still engage in other lawful defensive cyber operations otherwise permitted to them, but that any activity authorized by the Program must be conducted subject to the oversight, operational control, and legal authorities of the United States Government;

(xiii)  include procedures for evaluating each Participating Company for continued participation in the Program on at least an annual basis; and

(xiv)   mandate that the Program Executive Directors review every cyber operations package and provide written approval and direction to the Participating Company before action may be taken.

(b)  The Program Executive Directors shall regularly assess and continuously improve the Program’s operational procedures to maintain effective and efficient execution of the objectives outlined in this memorandum.  The NCC shall likewise utilize automation to streamline Program elements wherever appropriate, in accordance with applicable law and the requirements of this memorandum.

(c)  The Program Executive Directors shall, within 180 days of the date of this memorandum and annually thereafter, produce a report detailing the status of the Program and submit it to the Assistant to the President and Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy and Homeland Security Advisor and the National Cyber Director. 

Sec. 4.  Definitions.  For purposes of this memorandum:

(a)  “Cyber Effects Operation” means activity conducted in or through the interdependent network of information technology infrastructure that includes the Internet, telecommunications networks, computers, information systems, industrial control systems, networks, and embedded processors and controllers that results in the manipulation, disruption, denial, degradation, or destruction of information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon.

(b)  “Critical Outcomes.”  An action will be considered to generate a Critical Outcome if it is likely that it will: 

(i)   result in the loss of life or serious injury; or

(ii)  rise to the level of use of force or armed attack under international law.

(c)  “Cyber-Enabled Transnational Criminal Organization (CE-TCO)” means any foreign group that conducts cyber-enabled crime against the United States Government, a United States person, or United States interests, and that is not an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction.  For the purposes of this memorandum, a foreign group will be assumed not to be an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction unless clear intelligence exists establishing such connection.

(d)  “Cyber Surveillance Operation” means activities conducted in or through the interdependent network of information systems that includes the Internet, telecommunications networks, computers, information systems, industrial control systems, networks, and embedded processors and controllers for the primary purpose of collecting information or intelligence — including information that can be used for future Cyber Effects Operations — from information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon, with the intent to remain undetected.  Cyber Surveillance Operations entail accessing such information systems without authorization from the owner or operator or by exceeding authorized access.  Cyber Surveillance Operations include those actions essential and inherent to enabling Cyber Surveillance Operations, such as manipulation or temporary disruption that is not intended to cause physical effects or impact the usability of physical or virtual infrastructure.

(e)  “Information system” has the same meaning as it has in section 3502 of title 44, United States Code.

(f)  “Participating Companies” means private United States companies that have been accepted into the Program and will be authorized to conduct cyber operations under the direction of the United States Government.

(g)  “United States person” has the same meaning as it has in Executive Order 12333.

Sec. 5.  General Provisions.  (a)  Nothing in this memorandum shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:

(i)   the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or

(ii)  the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(b)  This memorandum shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

(c)  This memorandum is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

sentences.zh: 通过与接受联邦政府指导和监督的经过审查的美国公司合作，我们将增强应对 TCO 威胁以及打击针对美国公民的跨国网络犯罪、欺诈和其他掠夺性计划的能力。

blocks.html_en: Sec. 2.  Establishing the Program.  (a)  The National Coordination Center (NCC), established pursuant to section 6(d) of Executive Order 14159 of January 20, 2025 (Protecting the American People Against Invasion), shall create, manage, and maintain a Program to authorize Participating Companies, as defined in section 4(f) of this memorandum, to conduct Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations against foreign Cyber-Enabled Transnational Criminal Organizations (CE-TCOs), under the control and oversight of the Federal Government.  As part of lawful investigatory, protective, or intelligence operations carried out by Federal law enforcement, this Program shall:

sentences.en: Sec.
sentences.zh: 秒。

sentences.en: Establishing the Program.
sentences.zh: 制定计划。

sentences.en: (a) The National Coordination Center (NCC), established pursuant to section 6(d) of Executive Order 14159 of January 20, 2025 (Protecting the American People Against Invasion), shall create, manage, and maintain a Program to authorize Participating Companies, as defined in section 4(f) of this memorandum, to conduct Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations against foreign Cyber-Enabled Transnational Criminal Organizations (CE-TCOs), under the control and oversight of the Federal Government.
sentences.zh: (a) 根据 2025 年 1 月 20 日第 14159 号行政命令第 6(d) 节（保护美国人民免受入侵）成立的国家协调中心 (NCC) 应创建、管理和维护一项计划，以授权本备忘录第 4(f) 节中定义的参与公司针对外国网络驱动的跨国犯罪组织开展网络监视行动和网络效应行动（CE-TCO），受联邦政府的控制和监督。

sentences.en: As part of lawful investigatory, protective, or intelligence operations carried out by Federal law enforcement, this Program shall:
sentences.zh: 作为联邦执法部门开展的合法调查、保护或情报行动的一部分，本计划应：

blocks.html_en: (i)    be overseen by co-Executive Directors, one from the Department of Justice, designated by the Attorney General, and one from the Department of Homeland Security, designated by the Secretary of Homeland Security (Program Executive Directors).  The Program Executive Directors shall be delegated authority to approve, after coordination with each other, cyber operations conducted within the Program by personnel of their respective departments, except that they may not approve operations resulting in Critical Outcomes, as defined in section 4(b) of this memorandum.  Cyber operations shall only be approved after coordination between the Program Executive Directors, and any resulting operational action will be exclusively conducted on behalf of and under the supervision of the Federal Government pursuant to the Federal Government’s lawful authorities;

sentences.en: (i) be overseen by co-Executive Directors, one from the Department of Justice, designated by the Attorney General, and one from the Department of Homeland Security, designated by the Secretary of Homeland Security (Program Executive Directors).
sentences.zh: (i) 受联合执行董事监督，其中一名来自司法部，由总检察长指定，另一名来自国土安全部，由国土安全部部长指定（项目执行董事）。

sentences.en: The Program Executive Directors shall be delegated authority to approve, after coordination with each other, cyber operations conducted within the Program by personnel of their respective departments, except that they may not approve operations resulting in Critical Outcomes, as defined in section 4(b) of this memorandum.
sentences.zh: 项目执行董事应被授权在相互协调后批准各自部门人员在该项目内开展的网络行动，但他们不得批准导致本备忘录第 4(b) 节定义的关键成果的行动。

sentences.en: Cyber operations shall only be approved after coordination between the Program Executive Directors, and any resulting operational action will be exclusively conducted on behalf of and under the supervision of the Federal Government pursuant to the Federal Government’s lawful authorities;
sentences.zh: 网络运营只有在计划执行董事之间协调后才能获得批准，任何由此产生的运营行动将根据联邦政府的合法授权专门代表联邦政府并在联邦政府的监督下进行；

blocks.html_en: (ii)   require Participating Companies to enter into contractual agreements with the Department of Justice or the Department of Homeland Security, which shall ensure that Participating Companies undergo rigorous vetting and that their performance adheres to the strict operational procedures outlined in the implementation guidance directed in section 3 of this memorandum; and

sentences.en: (ii) require Participating Companies to enter into contractual agreements with the Department of Justice or the Department of Homeland Security, which shall ensure that Participating Companies undergo rigorous vetting and that their performance adheres to the strict operational procedures outlined in the implementation guidance directed in section 3 of this memorandum; and
sentences.zh: (ii) 要求参与公司与司法部或国土安全部签订合同协议，以确保参与公司经过严格审查，并确保其绩效遵守本备忘录第 3 节所述实施指南中概述的严格操作程序；和

blocks.html_en: (iii)  permit Participating Companies to enter into commercial agreements with:

sentences.en: (iii) permit Participating Companies to enter into commercial agreements with:
sentences.zh: (iii) 允许参与公司与以下机构签订商业协议：

blocks.html_en: (A)  private sector entities, from which the Participating Companies may receive for the purpose of proposing responsive cyber operations to the NCC any threat information collected in the course of those entities’ normal business activities; and

blocks.html_en: (B)  Federal, State, local, tribal, and territorial agencies, which will identify CE-TCO threats to the Participating Companies in a manner that enables them to propose cyber operations to the NCC that address those threats.

sentences.en: (B) Federal, State, local, tribal, and territorial agencies, which will identify CE-TCO threats to the Participating Companies in a manner that enables them to propose cyber operations to the NCC that address those threats.

blocks.html_en: (b)  The NCC shall conduct all Program activities in accordance with the Constitution and all other applicable laws and international obligations of the United States, including section 1030 of title 18, United States Code, thereby ensuring that Participating Companies are acting under the control and oversight of the United States Government.

sentences.en: (b) The NCC shall conduct all Program activities in accordance with the Constitution and all other applicable laws and international obligations of the United States, including section 1030 of title 18, United States Code, thereby ensuring that Participating Companies are acting under the control and oversight of the United States Government.
sentences.zh: (b) NCC 应根据美国宪法和所有其他适用法律和国际义务（包括《美国法典》第 18 章第 1030 条）开展所有计划活动，从而确保参与公司在美国政府的控制和监督下行事。

blocks.html_en: Sec. 3.  Implementing Guidance.  (a)  Within 60 days of the date of this memorandum, the Program Executive Directors shall, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, establish consensus operating procedures for the Program that ensure the Federal Government’s complete oversight and control of Participating Companies’ performance.  No operation may be approved unless it complies with these operating procedures.  The procedures shall:

sentences.en: Sec.
sentences.zh: 秒。

sentences.en: Implementing Guidance.
sentences.zh: 实施指南。

sentences.en: (a) Within 60 days of the date of this memorandum, the Program Executive Directors shall, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, establish consensus operating procedures for the Program that ensure the Federal Government’s complete oversight and control of Participating Companies’ performance.
sentences.zh: (a) 在本备忘录签署之日起 60 天内，计划执行董事应与国土安全委员会协调，为该计划制定一致的操作程序，以确保联邦政府对参与公司的绩效进行全面监督和控制。

sentences.en: No operation may be approved unless it complies with these operating procedures.
sentences.zh: 除非符合这些操作程序，否则不得批准任何操作。

sentences.en: The procedures shall:
sentences.zh: 程序应：

blocks.html_en: (i)     establish minimum standards that Participating Companies must meet in order to take part in the Program, which shall include appropriate levels of technical proficiency, proven performance of cyber operations, facility security, personnel vetting, competence, reliability, and other factors that the Program Executive Directors, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, determine are relevant or necessary for guaranteeing high confidence in a Participating Company’s ability to perform successfully in the Program;

sentences.en: (i) establish minimum standards that Participating Companies must meet in order to take part in the Program, which shall include appropriate levels of technical proficiency, proven performance of cyber operations, facility security, personnel vetting, competence, reliability, and other factors that the Program Executive Directors, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, determine are relevant or necessary for guaranteeing high confidence in a Participating Company’s ability to perform successfully in the Program;
sentences.zh: (i) 制定参与公司参与该计划必须满足的最低标准，其中应包括适当的技术熟练程度、经过验证的网络运营绩效、设施安全、人员审查、能力、可靠性以及计划执行董事与国土安全委员会协调确定的相关或必要的其他因素，以确保参与公司在该计划中成功执行的能力具有高度信心；

blocks.html_en: (ii)    ensure that the Program’s eligibility criteria enable participation by both large companies, which provide critical capacity, and smaller, more agile companies, which may be better suited for specialized or discrete tasks;

sentences.en: (ii) ensure that the Program’s eligibility criteria enable participation by both large companies, which provide critical capacity, and smaller, more agile companies, which may be better suited for specialized or discrete tasks;
sentences.zh: (ii) 确保该计划的资格标准能够让提供关键能力的大公司和可能更适合专门或离散任务的规模较小、更敏捷的公司参与；

blocks.html_en: (iii)   mandate that Participating Companies disclose to the NCC all contractual relationships entered into pursuant to section 2(a)(iii) of this memorandum;

sentences.en: (iii) mandate that Participating Companies disclose to the NCC all contractual relationships entered into pursuant to section 2(a)(iii) of this memorandum;
sentences.zh: (iii) 要求参与公司向 NCC 披露根据本备忘录第 2(a)(iii) 节订立的所有合同关系；

blocks.html_en: (iv)    authorize the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security to mandate as a condition of their contractual agreements with Participating Companies under section 2(a)(ii) of this memorandum that such companies maintain a bond or escrow in an amount not less than $1 million, to be forfeited should the Participating Company enter non‑compliance with its contractual agreement described in section 2(a)(ii) of this memorandum;

sentences.en: (iv) authorize the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security to mandate as a condition of their contractual agreements with Participating Companies under section 2(a)(ii) of this memorandum that such companies maintain a bond or escrow in an amount not less than $1 million, to be forfeited should the Participating Company enter non‑compliance with its contractual agreement described in section 2(a)(ii) of this memorandum;
sentences.zh: (iv) 授权司法部和国土安全部根据本备忘录第 2(a)(ii) 节规定，作为其与参与公司签订合同协议的条件，要求这些公司保留金额不少于 100 万美元的保证金或托管资金，如果参与公司不遵守本备忘录第 2(a)(ii) 节中所述的合同协议，则该保证金或托管资金将被没收；

sentences.en: (v) in conformance with the classified annex to this memorandum, set forth the operational workflow of the Program, which shall include operational deconfliction across Federal law enforcement, the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, the Department of War, the Department of Justice, and the United States Intelligence Community;

sentences.en: (vii) set forth standardized rubrics and templates for target identification and the creation and processing of Cyber Surveillance and Cyber Effects Operations packages;
sentences.zh: (vii) 制定用于目标识别以及网络监视和网络效应行动包的创建和处理的标准化规则和模板；

sentences.en: (x) include procedures to ensure that a Participating Company that discovers operational activity exceeding the parameters and restrictions of the cyber operation approved by the Program Executive Directors — such as unintentional targeting of (1) a United States person, (2) an information system residing in the United States, or (3) an information system under the control of a United States person — shall cease such operation, conduct minimization procedures, and immediately notify the NCC, which shall notify the Department of Justice;

sentences.en: (xiii) include procedures for evaluating each Participating Company for continued participation in the Program on at least an annual basis; and

blocks.html_en: Sec. 4.  Definitions.  For purposes of this memorandum:

sentences.en: Sec.
sentences.zh: 秒。

sentences.en: Definitions.
sentences.zh: 定义。

sentences.en: For purposes of this memorandum:
sentences.zh: 就本备忘录而言：

blocks.html_en: (a)  “Cyber Effects Operation” means activity conducted in or through the interdependent network of information technology infrastructure that includes the Internet, telecommunications networks, computers, information systems, industrial control systems, networks, and embedded processors and controllers that results in the manipulation, disruption, denial, degradation, or destruction of information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon.

sentences.en: (a) “Cyber Effects Operation” means activity conducted in or through the interdependent network of information technology infrastructure that includes the Internet, telecommunications networks, computers, information systems, industrial control systems, networks, and embedded processors and controllers that results in the manipulation, disruption, denial, degradation, or destruction of information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon.
sentences.zh: (a) “网络效应操作”是指在相互依存的信息技术基础设施网络中或通过信息技术基础设施网络进行的活动，这些基础设施包括互联网、电信网络、计算机、信息系统、工业控制系统、网络以及嵌入式处理器和控制器，导致对信息系统、网络、信息系统控制的物理或虚拟基础设施或其中驻留的信息进行操纵、破坏、拒绝、降级或破坏。

blocks.html_en: (b)  “Critical Outcomes.”  An action will be considered to generate a Critical Outcome if it is likely that it will:

sentences.en: (b) “Critical Outcomes.”
sentences.zh: (b) “关键成果”。

sentences.en: An action will be considered to generate a Critical Outcome if it is likely that it will:
sentences.zh: 如果一项行动可能会出现以下情况，则该行动将被视为产生关键结果：

blocks.html_en: (i)   result in the loss of life or serious injury; or

sentences.en: (i) result in the loss of life or serious injury; or
sentences.zh: (i) 导致生命损失或严重伤害；或者

blocks.html_en: (ii)  rise to the level of use of force or armed attack under international law.

sentences.en: (ii) rise to the level of use of force or armed attack under international law.
sentences.zh: (ii) 上升到国际法规定的使用武力或武装攻击的程度。

blocks.html_en: (c)  “Cyber-Enabled Transnational Criminal Organization (CE-TCO)” means any foreign group that conducts cyber-enabled crime against the United States Government, a United States person, or United States interests, and that is not an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction.  For the purposes of this memorandum, a foreign group will be assumed not to be an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction unless clear intelligence exists establishing such connection.

sentences.en: (c) “Cyber-Enabled Transnational Criminal Organization (CE-TCO)” means any foreign group that conducts cyber-enabled crime against the United States Government, a United States person, or United States interests, and that is not an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction.
sentences.zh: (c) “网络跨国犯罪组织 (CE-TCO)”是指针对美国政府、美国人或美国利益实施网络犯罪的任何外国组织，该组织不是外国政府的机构组成部分，也不是完全在外国政府的指导下运作。

sentences.en: For the purposes of this memorandum, a foreign group will be assumed not to be an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction unless clear intelligence exists establishing such connection.

blocks.html_en: (d)  “Cyber Surveillance Operation” means activities conducted in or through the interdependent network of information systems that includes the Internet, telecommunications networks, computers, information systems, industrial control systems, networks, and embedded processors and controllers for the primary purpose of collecting information or intelligence — including information that can be used for future Cyber Effects Operations — from information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon, with the intent to remain undetected.  Cyber Surveillance Operations entail accessing such information systems without authorization from the owner or operator or by exceeding authorized access.  Cyber Surveillance Operations include those actions essential and inherent to enabling Cyber Surveillance Operations, such as manipulation or temporary disruption that is not intended to cause physical effects or impact the usability of physical or virtual infrastructure.

副总统备忘录

国务卿

财政部长

总统助理兼办公厅主任

国家情报总监

总统科学技术助理

中央情报局局长

管理和预算办公室主任

总统国家安全事务助理

总统助理兼政策副参谋长和国土安全顾问

国家网络总监

参谋长联席会议主席

国家安全局局长

根据美利坚合众国宪法和法律赋予我的总统权力，我特此指示如下：

第 1 节。 目的。 跨国犯罪组织 (TCO) 对美国公民、企业和国家安全构成越来越大的威胁。 这些组织开展持续的网络活动，实施破坏美国繁荣、安全和自由的欺诈行为。 通过 2026 年 3 月 6 日第 14390 号行政命令（打击针对美国公民的网络犯罪、欺诈和掠夺性计划），我指示联邦政府采取各种行动，打击危害美国公民的网络犯罪。 该备忘录通过结合私营部门的聪明才智，扩大了对 TCO 实施的网络犯罪的打击范围。

美国私营部门是世界上最具创新性和技术最先进的，其规模、速度和能力确保了美国的关键进攻性网络优势。 然而，美国企业的创新能力历来在识别和破坏网络空间犯罪网络方面并未得到充分利用。 因此，美国的政策是利用一切国家力量手段，包括私营部门的创新能力，打击网络犯罪。 通过与接受联邦政府指导和监督的经过审查的美国公司合作，我们将增强应对 TCO 威胁以及打击针对美国公民的跨国网络犯罪、欺诈和其他掠夺性计划的能力。

秒。 2. 制定计划。 (a) 根据 2025 年 1 月 20 日第 14159 号行政命令第 6(d) 节（保护美国人民免受入侵）成立的国家协调中心 (NCC) 应创建、管理和维护一项计划，以授权本备忘录第 4(f) 节中定义的参与公司针对外国网络驱动的跨国犯罪组织开展网络监视行动和网络效应行动（CE-TCO），受联邦政府的控制和监督。 作为联邦执法部门开展的合法调查、保护或情报行动的一部分，本计划应：

(i) 受联合执行董事监督，其中一名来自司法部，由总检察长指定，另一名来自国土安全部，由国土安全部部长指定（项目执行董事）。 项目执行董事应被授权在相互协调后批准各自部门人员在该项目内开展的网络行动，但他们不得批准导致本备忘录第 4(b) 节定义的关键成果的行动。 网络运营只有在计划执行董事之间协调后才能获得批准，任何由此产生的运营行动将根据联邦政府的合法授权专门代表联邦政府并在联邦政府的监督下进行；

(ii) 要求参与公司与司法部或国土安全部签订合同协议，以确保参与公司经过严格审查，并确保其绩效遵守本备忘录第 3 节所述实施指南中概述的严格操作程序；和

(iii) 允许参与公司与以下机构签订商业协议：

(A) 私营部门实体，参与公司可以从私营部门实体接收在这些实体正常业务活动过程中收集的任何威胁信息，以便向 NCC 提出响应性网络操作；和

(B) 联邦、州、地方、部落和地区机构，它们将识别 CE-TCO 对参与公司的威胁，使他们能够向 NCC 提出解决这些威胁的网络操作建议。

(b) NCC 应根据美国宪法和所有其他适用法律和国际义务（包括《美国法典》第 18 章第 1030 条）开展所有计划活动，从而确保参与公司在美国政府的控制和监督下行事。

秒。 3. 实施指南。 (a) 在本备忘录签署之日起 60 天内，计划执行董事应与国土安全委员会协调，为该计划制定一致的操作程序，以确保联邦政府对参与公司的绩效进行全面监督和控制。 除非符合这些操作程序，否则不得批准任何操作。 程序应：

(i) 制定参与公司参与该计划必须满足的最低标准，其中应包括适当的技术熟练程度、经过验证的网络运营绩效、设施安全、人员审查、能力、可靠性以及计划执行董事与国土安全委员会协调确定的相关或必要的其他因素，以确保参与公司在该计划中成功执行的能力具有高度信心；

(ii) 确保该计划的资格标准能够让提供关键能力的大公司和可能更适合专门或离散任务的规模较小、更敏捷的公司参与；

(iii) 要求参与公司向 NCC 披露根据本备忘录第 2(a)(iii) 节订立的所有合同关系；

(iv) 授权司法部和国土安全部根据本备忘录第 2(a)(ii) 节规定，作为其与参与公司签订合同协议的条件，要求这些公司保留金额不少于 100 万美元的保证金或托管资金，如果参与公司不遵守本备忘录第 2(a)(ii) 节中所述的合同协议，则该保证金或托管资金将被没收；

(v) 根据本备忘录的机密附件，规定该计划的运作流程，其中应包括联邦执法部门、国务院、财政部、陆军部、司法部和美国情报界之间的运作冲突消除；

(vi) 根据本备忘录的分类附件，提供一个裁决框架，以确保业务活动仅针对 CE-TCO 并考虑其他美国政府股权；

(vii) 制定用于目标识别以及网络监视和网络效应行动包的创建和处理的标准化规则和模板；

(viii) 包括对参与公司的报告要求，这将有助于更好地了解外国 CE-TCO 的活动和影响，特别是与美国人民和经济相关的活动和影响，并确保 NCC 充分了解参与公司的运营活动；

(ix) 包括程序，包括司法部的审查，以确保任何针对美国人或以其他方式涉及美国政府根据宪法、联邦法或国际法承担的义务的计划活动在批准行动之前获得任何必要的司法或其他授权；

(x) 制定程序，确保参与公司发现运营活动超出计划执行董事批准的网络运营参数和限制，例如无意中针对 (1) 美国人、(2) 居住在美国的信息系统或 (3) 美国人控制下的信息系统，应停止此类运营，执行最小化程序，并立即通知 NCC，NCC 应通知司法部；

(xi) 纳入程序，要求参与公司在发现美国关键基础设施即将遭受网络攻击或有合理理由相信批准的网络效应行动或网络监视行动可能导致重大结果时，立即通知 NCC，NCC 又应通知司法部；

(xii) 澄清参与公司仍可从事其允许的其他合法防御性网络行动，但该计划授权的任何活动必须在美国政府的监督、运营控制和法律授权下进行；

(xiii) 包括至少每年评估每个参与公司是否继续参与该计划的程序；和

(xiv) 要求计划执行董事审查每个网络运营方案，并在采取行动之前向参与公司提供书面批准和指示。

(b) 计划执行董事应定期评估并持续改进计划的运作程序，以保持有效且高效地执行本备忘录中概述的目标。 NCC 同样应根据适用法律和本备忘录的要求，在适当的情况下利用自动化来简化计划要素。

(c) 计划执行董事应在本备忘录发布之日起 180 天内以及此后每年编写一份报告，详细说明该计划的状况，并将其提交给总统助理、负责政策和国土安全顾问的副参谋长以及国家网络主任。

秒。 4. 定义。 就本备忘录而言：

(a) “网络效应操作”是指在相互依存的信息技术基础设施网络中或通过信息技术基础设施网络进行的活动，这些基础设施包括互联网、电信网络、计算机、信息系统、工业控制系统、网络以及嵌入式处理器和控制器，导致对信息系统、网络、信息系统控制的物理或虚拟基础设施或其中驻留的信息进行操纵、破坏、拒绝、降级或破坏。

(b) “关键成果”。 如果一项行动可能会出现以下情况，则该行动将被视为产生关键结果：

(i) 导致生命损失或严重伤害；或者

(ii) 上升到国际法规定的使用武力或武装攻击的程度。

(c) “网络跨国犯罪组织 (CE-TCO)”是指针对美国政府、美国人或美国利益实施网络犯罪的任何外国组织，该组织不是外国政府的机构组成部分，也不是完全在外国政府的指导下运作。 就本备忘录而言，外国集团将被视为不是外国政府的机构组成部分，也不是完全在外国政府的指导下运作，除非存在明确的情报证明存在这种联系。

(d) “网络监视行动”是指在相互依存的信息系统网络中进行的活动，包括互联网、电信网络、计算机、信息系统、工业控制系统、网络以及嵌入式处理器和控制器，其主要目的是从信息系统、网络、信息系统控制的物理或虚拟基础设施或其中驻留的信息收集信息或情报（包括可用于未来网络效应行动的信息），目的是不被发现。 网络监视操作需要在未经所有者或运营商授权或超出授权访问的情况下访问此类信息系统。 网络监视操作包括实现网络监视操作所必需和固有的那些操作，例如无意造成物理影响或影响物理或虚拟基础设施可用性的操纵或临时中断。

(e) “信息系统”的含义与《美国法典》第 44 章第 3502 条中的含义相同。

(f) “参与公司”是指已获准加入该计划并将被授权在美国政府指导下开展网络运营的美国私营公司。

(g) “美国人”的含义与第 12333 号行政命令中的含义相同。

秒。 5. 一般规定。 (a) 本备忘录中的任何内容均不得被解释为损害或以其他方式影响：

(i) 法律授予执行部门或机构或其负责人的权力；或者

(ii) 管理和预算办公室主任与预算、行政或立法提案有关的职能。

(b) 本备忘录的实施应符合适用法律并视拨款情况而定。

(c) 本备忘录无意且不会创造任何实体或程序性的、可由任何一方根据法律或衡平法强制执行的针对美国、其部门、机构或实体、其官员、雇员或代理人或任何其他人的任何权利或利益。
